# Pending changes (since patch 0013, 2026-11-20)

## 2026-11-20 - Fix: nebulae snapping in and out of existence

Asked: "nebula seems to snap in and out of existance".
Found: the space backdrop's Nebulae layer (main.tscn, a Parallax2D at 6% of the camera's scroll) repeated every 3200 px
(twice each way), but a system's 2-3 nebulae are 800-1900 px each, placed from -1600 to +1400: together about 4900 px.
A repeating layer wraps its offset round at the tile size, so as you flew (most visibly zoomed out - a 0.6 zoom shows
3200 x 1800 of it) the part of the backdrop past the tile jumped a whole tile: pieces of nebula popped in and out.
Measured by flying the ship across a system with everything but the nebulae hidden and comparing each frame's
brightness: 2 jumps of 13-15% per pass at zoom 0.6 before, none at 0.6 / 1.0 / 1.6 on three passes after.
Done: the Nebulae layer no longer repeats (it scrolls at 6% and the nebulae stay where they are); a comment in main.gd
says why.
Files: main.tscn, scripts/main.gd.

## 2026-11-20 - The game in a browser and on phones; Linux and Windows builds

Asked: make the game web friendly to publish on itch.io as a web game, optimised for mobile phones too (the right
render engine etc.), with Linux and Windows downloads.
Done:
- Export presets (export_presets.cfg): Linux (x86_64, one file with the data inside), Windows (x86_64, one .exe;
  no resource editing - that needs rcedit) and **Web**: (first single-threaded; now multi-threaded - see the next section), textures for desktop and mobile GPUs
  (S3TC/BPTC and ETC2/ASTC), the canvas filling the page. All three carry the game's JSON / Markdown / text data
  (include_filter) and leave out external/, tests/ and tools/.
- The renderer: Forward+ on desktops as before; **Compatibility** (OpenGL ES 3 / WebGL 2) on the web and on mobile
  (project.godot rendering_method.web / .mobile) - the only one a browser runs. Every doc-shot moment (27: space,
  combat, mining, stations, every computer page, the Repair Bay, surgery, the surface) was taken under it on the
  desktop: no errors, the same look.
- Size: the web download's data was 214 MB; the automaton's four anatomy pictures (4096 px, 10 MB each on the card,
  twice - desktop and mobile formats) were 81 MB of it. The web build now carries half-size copies (art/anatomy/web/,
  2048 px, 2.5 MB each on the card - kinder to a phone's memory too): AnatomyArt.path() picks them on the web,
  AnatomyArt.region() scales the surgery table's picture rectangles to them (the UV-drawn patches already were);
  each build leaves out the other's set. Web data now 153 MB (138 MB zipped, the engine 39.5 MB more).
- **Touch** (TouchControls, autoload "Touch"): a tap is a click (Godot's mouse emulation - fly, walk, hold to keep
  going, hold on a rock to cut it); a quick **two-finger tap** is the right button (scan, the probe scanner, the
  context menu on foot); a **pinch** zooms; two columns of buttons by the left edge - MENU, COMPUTER, MAP, ATTACK,
  DOCK, ZOOM + / - - between the status bars and the event log (the right side has the minimap, the quest and the
  planet panel). Shown with a touch screen, in play, and not while a menu covers the game.
- On the web (Settings.on_web): no window sizing (the page owns it), no Exit button, no Resolution row; on a phone's
  first run the text starts a size up (Settings.PHONE_TEXT: HUD and dialogue 1.3, menus 1.25, the world 1.2).
- A stale converted scene in the export cache made the web build warn about station_menu.tscn's script UID: cleared.
- Checked in a real browser (Chromium, WebGL 2): the attract mode, the title screen, a new game in space at 60 FPS
  (the browser's cap), no errors; as an Android phone (915 x 412, touch): taps start the game and fly, the touch
  buttons show and COMPUTER opens the Ship Computer. The Linux build runs; the Windows build runs under Wine.
- Docs: game.md's Controls has a paragraph on playing by touch.
- Tests: test_touch (the buttons in play and hidden under a menu, the zoom buttons and a pinch, a two-finger tap
  opening the probe scanner's map, the web bits: phone text, the anatomy paths and regions).
Files: export_presets.cfg, project.godot, scripts/touch_controls.gd (new), scripts/settings.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd,
scripts/anatomy_art.gd, scripts/surgery.gd, art/anatomy/web/*.png (new), data/docs/game.md, tests/test_touch.gd (new).

## 2026-11-20 - The web version: sound, smooth planets (threads); the mining panel; no FPS meter for players; no title flash

Asked: "audio is missing in the web version", "when i abandon mining the mining ui still stays on", "the release
version not to have fps meter on by default including its graph", "when the game first loads it displays asteroid
sprites for a second or two in the main menu", "make sure the game runs smoothly ... lag spikes, especially when i
was on a planet, also the audio seems to crack a bit", "the frame rate also seemed very low".
Found and done:
- **No sound on the web**: the web build played sounds the Web Audio "sample" way (Godot's default there), which
  didn't take the game's own buses (Music / SFX / Voice, made at start). project.godot
  audio/general/default_playback_type.web = Stream: the game mixes its sound itself, as on the desktop. Measured in
  Chromium with the page's audio output tapped: the title and space went from silence (peak 0) to peaks of ~0.24.
- **Spikes on planets, crackling, a low frame rate on the web**: the web build was single-threaded, so everything the
  desktop game does on worker threads (a planet's ground, scenery and paths streamed as you walk, pictures loading)
  ran in the frame, and so did the sound's mixing (a long frame starved it: the crackles). Measured in Chromium
  (60 Hz screen, the game played by a script: start, land on Amnissos, walk): single-threaded - landing's worst frame
  5066 ms, walking's 1533 ms (55.5 fps average); multi-threaded - landing 283 ms, walking 50 ms (59.6 fps, steady).
  The Web preset now has thread support on (itch.io: its "SharedArrayBuffer support" switch, on for the page).
- **Landing's long frame** (desktop too): 45-56 ms -> 31-34 ms. The tile set's cached scenery pictures are decoded on
  a worker while the planet is made (TerrainTiles.predecode; their first drawing decoded a dozen PNGs in that
  frame: ~6 ms); the CanvasLayers to show are listed when the surface is built, not searched for (5000+ nodes) in
  the frame it appears; the animals, the map's fog and the scenery placing start a moment after (not in that frame).
- **The mining panel** showed for as long as a rock was your target (within 2600 px): now while you hold the button
  on it (or the autopilot mines), and LINGER (3 s) after the laser last cut (Ship.mining_at), within REACH (1400).
- **The FPS meter** (and its graph) is off by default in exported builds (Settings.fps_counter_default(): not
  OS.has_feature("template")); still on when run from the project. The guide says so.
- **The title screen's flash of asteroids** (and a planet, a station's outline) for a second at the first start: the
  Warmup drew one of everything "nearly clear" (modulate alpha 0.02) - but pictures drawn with premultiplied alpha
  (the rocks through ShaderCache, planets, stations) ignore a modulate's alpha. Now the Warmup is dark as well as
  clear, and on a CanvasLayer under an opaque cover in the backdrop's colour, below the star field, for its few
  frames (still drawn - pipelines made - unseen). Checked on a recording of the first seconds; a new game's longest
  frame unchanged (28-31 ms).
- Tests: test_mining_industry.test_mining_panel_only_while_mining (new), test_fps_counter (the default), test_fog
  (the reveal a moment after landing).
Files: project.godot, export_presets.cfg, scripts/mining_panel.gd, scripts/ship.gd, scripts/hud.gd,
scripts/settings.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd, scripts/warmup.gd, scripts/terrain_tiles.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd,
data/docs/game.md, tests/test_mining_industry.gd, tests/test_fps_counter.gd, tests/test_fog.gd.

## 2026-11-20 - The title screen opens at once; the art loads behind it

Asked: why the web version takes so long to load before the main menu; then "option 1" (load what the title screen
needs, the rest in the background).
Found: the start-up loading screen waited for every sprite (1093 pictures, 82 MB: ProcArt), the Minoan building
textures and four scenes before opening the menu. In a browser (fewer threads, decoding in WebAssembly) that was
17-65 s after the download (65 s cold).
Done: the loading screen loads only the title screen's scene and opens it (LoadingScreen.SCENES; LATER: the space,
surface and station scenes); ProcArt keeps loading the sprites and, one after another, those scenes behind the menu
(ProcArt.load_scenes, scenes_done, all_ready(), wait_ready(), overall()). Whatever needs them waits: a new game or a
loaded save (LoadVeil: its bar's first half is the art, its text what's loading; its time-out held meanwhile),
attract mode (not before), Talos from the title (a "Loading the game's art: N%" note until it's in), the title's
Warmup (after the sprites). Measured in Chromium on a fresh profile, the build served locally: the menu at ~6-8 s
from opening the page (was 17-65 s); START GAME clicked as soon as it showed: space ~9 s later.
Files: scripts/loading_screen.gd, scripts/proc_art.gd, scripts/load_veil.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd.

## 2026-11-20 - No start-up loading screen; pictures load as you play, placeholders meanwhile

Asked: "it still take forever it gets stuck in loading screens"; "is there a way to completely remove loading screens and
instead make everything load in the background while the game plays"; "if something does not load in time just make a
placeholder asset and use that until it loads".
Found: on itch.io the tab froze for seconds at a time while the title screen waited for 1093 sprites, all requested at
once (Chromium's long tasks: up to 4.4 s at boot, then 0.3-1.7 s stalls); and in an exported game the sprite folder
was listed with DirAccess, which sees the imported pictures, not the PNGs - so the start-up list was nearly empty and
the sprites were loaded one by one, waiting, as the game asked for them.
Done:
- The game starts on the title screen (run/main_scene = main_menu.tscn); the loading screen (loading.tscn,
  loading_screen.gd) is gone. The title starts the other scenes loading behind it (ProcArt.load_scenes).
- ProcArt loads the sprites (listed with ResourceLoader.list_directory) three at a time, taking them in within 3 ms a
  frame, for the whole game (_process) - the asked-for ones first.
- ProcArt.sprite(key): a sprite to draw - one not in yet comes as a placeholder of its size (data/sprites/sizes.json,
  tools/sprite_sizes.py): a soft, faint shape; its picture replaces it in place when it's in (ImageTexture.set_image:
  the same texture, the same RID - whatever holds it shows the real thing). Used by ships (yours, NPCs: EnemyTypes),
  stations. ProcArt.get_tex(key) stays the real picture always (loaded at once if needed, filling a placeholder) -
  for what reads pixels or bakes atlases and tile caches.
- Nothing waits for the art any more: a new game, a loaded save, attract mode (only Talos from the title waits - it
  shows every picture).
- Measured in Chromium (the build served locally): the menu at ~1 s; START GAME then: space ~9 s later (the galaxy
  made and the system built under the "New game" veil), the ship a placeholder for ~2 s. Freezes over 200 ms: 4 (the
  engine's start 3.9 s, two of ~1.2 s as the first system is built).
- Tests: test_scripts (the start scene); test_frontier.test_bouncer_plasma sure shots (Accuracy.sure). All pass.
Files: project.godot, scripts/proc_art.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd, scripts/load_veil.gd, scripts/ship.gd,
scripts/station.gd, scripts/music.gd, tools/sprite_sizes.py (new), data/sprites/sizes.json (new),
loading.tscn and scripts/loading_screen.gd (removed), tests/test_scripts.gd, tests/test_frontier.gd.

## 2026-11-20 - A loading bar above the event log; planets built ahead, so landing doesn't freeze

Asked: "a small progress bar in game above the console that shows the progress of loading assets in the background ...
the same width as the console"; "landing on planet freezing the game - use placeholders there as well and everything
loaded in the background".
Found: landing waited for the whole surface - the planet made on a worker (~5 s), its ground (~2.4 s), buildings,
scenery and the pad's surroundings (~2 s): ~9-10 s on the desktop with the ship held at 92% shrunk, far longer in a
browser; and the surface's pictures could still be loaded on the spot.
Done:
- GameLog.LoadBar: a thin bar (18 px) just above the event log, as wide as it, hidden with it (L): "Loading assets N%"
  (ProcArt.overall) then "Preparing the surface of <planet> N%"; gone when nothing's loading.
- Planets built ahead (main.gd _prebuild_tick / _prebuild / _drop_prebuild): the nearest landable planet within
  PREBUILD_R (4000 px) gets its surface built hidden in the background while you fly (1 ms a frame of the main
  thread's work - PlanetSurface.background - the heavy part on its worker); landing on it takes it as it is
  (adopt_state: the game as it is now - credits, gear, your ship's picture redone if it changed) - the landing
  animation only. Flown off (beyond DROP_R 9000), another planet nearer, or leaving the system: dropped - a built
  one taken apart a few ms a frame; one still being built stops at its next stage and is taken apart from there
  (discard). The surface is given its planet and the game's state (planet_override, state_override), not
  SaveGame's (you aren't landed yet); its effects layer joins "fx_layer" only once shown; its lifts aren't worked
  out while hidden. Off in headless runs (prebuild_on) but test_play.test_surface_built_ahead.
- The surface's pictures first in the background loading (ProcArt.prefetch: its tile set's tiles and creatures);
  creatures, citizens, glows and bolts drawn with ProcArt.sprite (placeholders till they're in).
- ProcArt loads 8 sprites at once on a desktop (3 in a browser).
- Fix: quitting while a surface was being built never ended - the world's making reads pictures back on its worker,
  which waits for the renderer the main thread drives, and the main thread waited for it outright. Its tasks are
  now waited for while letting the renderer run (PlanetSurface._await_task: RenderingServer.force_sync while
  polling).
- Measured (desktop): assets 0 -> 100% in ~5 s after a new game, then Amnissos prepared ahead; landing on it then
  takes the animation only (test: < 6 s, was ~10); a jump's worst frame 25 ms (a half-built surface freed at once
  had been 343 ms); landing elsewhere (not built ahead) as before (worst ~40 ms).
- Docs: game.md (the bar, built-ahead planets). Tests: test_play.test_surface_built_ahead (new);
  test_hardpoints (a warship drawing an Electro/Bouncer instead of a loadout: another).
Files: scripts/event_log.gd, scripts/main.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd, scripts/proc_art.gd,
scripts/surface_creature.gd, scripts/surface_props.gd, data/docs/game.md, tests/test_play.gd, tests/test_hardpoints.gd.

## 2026-11-20 - The web version loads its pictures 5x faster; planets ready ~20 s into a system; the bar says what it does

Asked: "if it loads assets for solar system and i land on planet it just freezes for almost a minute, the planet should
load instantly after the landing animation"; "the loading bar should name specific which asset it loads or what kind
of processing it does".
Found (measured in Chromium, timing lines in the build): the browser loaded the 1093 sprites at ~15 a second - over 70
s in all - through the threaded loader, whose hand-overs to the main thread stalled it 1-2 s at a time and took the
worker threads the planet's making needs (that ran 14-23 s instead of ~8). A surface's build also fetched its tiles on
the spot (a 3.5 s frame), and once asked for every tile first, alphabetically, its own came last (74 s).
Done:
- In a browser ProcArt loads on the main thread, as many a frame as fit in 8 ms (WEB_BUDGET_US): all the art in ~13 s
  (was 70+), the planet's making back to ~8.6 s.
- ProcArt.ensure(prefixes): waits, frames going on, until those pictures are in (loaded first); prefetch keeps the
  order it's given. A surface asks for its own pictures first - its tile set, its creatures, its empire's
  architecture, the palace's, then the rest - waits for its ground tiles before the planet's making and for the rest
  after it: nothing loaded on the spot.
- Planets built ahead from the moment you're in a system (the nearest landable, however far; another only once it's
  well inside PREBUILD_R and less than half as far): ~20 s in (browser) / ~6 s (desktop), landing takes the
  animation only.
- The title's warm-up (the GPU's first-use work: a browser compiles each shader in a 1-2 s frame) starts at once again,
  pictures not in yet as placeholders - not after all the art (which put those frames into play).
- The bar above the event log: "Loading <what>: <which>  (n / 1093)" (ProcArt.stage, counts()), then "<Planet>: <step>
  N%" - Generating its terrain, Planning its villages and gates, Linking its land: ramps and causeways, Painting its
  ground and map, Loading its ground tiles / its buildings' and creatures' pictures, Laying its ground tiles, Raising
  its buildings and scenery, Finishing (PlanetSurface.build_stage) - for a planet built ahead or the landing under way.
- Tests: test_play.test_surface_built_ahead clears the home system's raiders first (no landing under attack).
Files: scripts/proc_art.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd, scripts/main.gd, scripts/main_menu.gd, scripts/event_log.gd,
tests/test_play.gd.

## 2026-11-20 - Planets made chunk by chunk: the ground streams in round you, a placeholder plate under it

Asked: "generate the planet in chunks not in one go, piece by piece, first the placeholder and as soon as the assets
are loaded then the assets replacing the placeholder but always chunk by chunk"; "everything happens on the background
nothing block user interaction"; chose the new chunked generator (planet layouts change; old saves' explored maps and
positions on planets reset).
Done:
- SurfacePlanner (new, scripts/surface_planner.gd, ~1100 lines): the planet's maker as units, each the same from its
  seed in any order. Planet constants (noise, the water's shape, the height range and the site level from a 1/8
  sample); terrain made lazily in 16x16 blocks; the plan (landing disc, the pad's village, a village per 110-tile
  region by chance - at least one in each quarter - industry, pirate bands, gates, village fauna) touching only the
  ground near what it plans; a chunk (32x32 tiles): heights tidied, plots and spots levelled, natural ramps, every
  level inside it linked by ramps (BFS), islands' causeways (a lattice), its tiles, its map pixels (hill-shaded), its
  creatures.
- The surface opens on the plan and the pad's chunks; the rest come on a worker, one at a time, nearest first, within
  3.6 chunks of you (more as you walk), taken in within 2.5 ms a frame (500 tiles a step; 1 ms for a planet built
  ahead). Under them a plate of the ground's colour; the ground pictures (GroundChunks.refresh) redrawn where a chunk
  lands. Buildings, citizens, gates, scenery and creatures come where their ground is in. A gate trip asks for the
  ground round the other gate first (stream_area).
- Nothing searched for when nothing near is left to make (the pump idles till you move a quarter chunk).
- Quitting while a planet's being made no longer hangs (a worker reading textures back waits on the renderer: the
  wait keeps it served - RenderingServer.force_sync).
- A temple with no free wall left gets its chest in place of a piece.
- Tests: those that look at the whole planet stream it all first (stream_all); frame-budget ones wait for the
  streaming to settle.
Numbers: chunk 32x32 tiles (196 on a 440-tile planet), ~3.6-chunk streaming radius, 2.5 ms take-in budget a frame.
Files: scripts/surface_planner.gd (new), scripts/planet_surface.gd, scripts/ground_chunks.gd, tests/test_surface.gd,
tests/test_frame_budget.gd, tests/test_gas_giant.gd, tests/test_volcanic.gd, data/docs/shots/surface_walk.jpg.

## 2026-11-20 - A memory pool for the loaded assets; the loading bar becomes a loading console

Asked: "create a memory pool that allows to maintain loaded assets, those assets will never be unloaded unless the
pool runs out of memory. The assets get a priority number that depends on how much the user uses those assets ...
The loading bar should have a report of the total memory used for the memory pool, reserve double that is usually
needed ... i want also the unloading to be reported, turn the asset progress bar to a console with a progress bar".
Done:
- AssetPool (new, scripts/asset_pool.gd): every loaded asset registered with its size - ProcArt's sprites (w x h x 4
  bytes: lossless, no mipmaps), their CPU copies (get_image), the four anatomy pictures (pinned: one costs a long frame
  to load again). Its room (budget) = 2 x the usual need (every sprite: 244 MB, plus the anatomy pictures) - 547 MB on
  desktop. Priority = uses, each use (sprite() / get_tex()) adding one, fading with a 5-minute half-life. Over budget it
  unloads the lowest-priority assets nothing else holds (a texture's reference count: one on screen stays) until it
  fits, and notes each ("Unloaded <name> (<MB>, priority <p>) - the pool was full").
- An unloaded sprite asked for again comes back as before: a placeholder of its size at once, the real picture
  loaded in the background (sprite() now does this whenever a picture isn't in, not only during the first load).
- The loading console (event_log.gd LoadBar): above the event log, as wide - its last 3 lines (loads in blue,
  unloads in orange, work in white: "Amnissos: planned - N villages...", "Amnissos: ground chunk 7,3 in (32 x 32
  tiles, 37 of 196)"), a progress bar (a planet built ahead; the ground being made round you on a planet -
  PlanetSurface.near_progress; the pictures loading) and the pool's line: "Memory pool 296.9 MB / 546.6 MB - 1395
  assets - none unloaded", with a thin gauge (orange over 90%). Shown while at work and 6 s after the last note.
- Guide (game.md): the console, the memory pool and the chunked planets.
- Tests: test_asset_pool (least used unloaded first, only when full; held and pinned ones never; unloads reported and
  counted; sprites in the pool; using one raises its priority).
Numbers: sprites 244 MB (1093), budget 547 MB, half-life 300 s, console 3 lines + bar + pool line (~82 px).
Files: scripts/asset_pool.gd (new), scripts/proc_art.gd, scripts/anatomy_art.gd, scripts/event_log.gd,
scripts/planet_surface.gd, data/docs/game.md, tests/test_asset_pool.gd (new), data/docs/shots.json (space_hud: a note for the console),
data/docs/shots/space_hud.jpg, surface_walk.jpg, surgery.jpg, archive.jpg (retaken).

## 2026-11-20 - No loading stalls in the first frames of a system, the Ship Computer or Talos

Asked: "everything happens on the background nothing block user interaction"; "no operation will be blocking in any
way the user from interacting with the game". (The space scene's own build - main.gd - is in its own section.)
Found (fps_test.py loading --profile, timings in a live window): a jump or a new game's build froze the scene ~0.6 s
at 60 Hz (a piece a frame, ~36 frames, nothing moving); the jump gates loaded 7 pictures on the spot (ProcArt.get_tex:
42 ms in a new game's build); the nav beacon's trail shader compiled in play (its first frame 70-140 ms: the title's
warm-up never drew one); the Ship Computer was made in one 40-60 ms frame; Talos over the game in a 35-40 ms frame.
Done:
- Pictures only drawn come as placeholders, never loaded on the spot (ProcArt.sprite instead of get_tex): the jump
  gates, the nav beacon, the minimap's ring and glass, a gas giant's sky, the ship on a landing pad, the station
  menu's ship picture.
- The title's warm-up draws a nav beacon too (its trail shader compiled there).
- The space scene's build: several pieces a frame within 3 ms, the scene running (you fly) while its pieces come into
  view, each still till it's shown; the ships and rocks of a system a piece at a time. (Measured: a new game's still
  time 595 -> ~190 ms, a jump 80-93 -> 61 ms.)
- The Ship Computer made ahead a piece a frame: its window, its inventory, then shown for two frames unseen (its
  layout and text done then, not at the first Tab), its slots' icons a few ms a frame, then the maps.
- Talos opens at once (its starfield), its data editor made over the next three frames (itself, its frame, its
  page); a tool picked meanwhile opens when it's ready.
- UI.dismantle (taking a scene apart a few ms a frame) never frees a node that's mid-call or out of the tree
  (queued for the end of the frame instead): taking off logged "Object is locked", and a surface dropped as the
  space scene closed crashed the game (a double free).
- Station missions: each offer's description at most two lines (all of it in the card's tooltip) - a station with
  long offers at 150% text made the page scroll.
Files: scripts/jump_gate.gd, scripts/nav_beacon.gd, scripts/minimap.gd, scripts/gas_sky.gd, scripts/surface_props.gd,
scripts/station_menu.gd, scripts/warmup.gd, scripts/ship_menu.gd, scripts/editor_screen.gd, scripts/ui.gd,

## 2026-11-20 - A solar system streams in piece by piece; every planet's surface built ahead; the loading console scrolls, folds and maps the memory pool

Asked: "when you load a solar system, load everything, planets, planet surfaces, stations, ships, monsters etc again
via streaming"; "the loading assets console should have a scroll bar like the event console, dont close it when
loading has finished"; "an arrow button that collapses it once clicked to just the progress bar"; "another bar ...
shows the map of the memory pool ... areas colored different ... a tooltip with detail stats about specific assets
consuming memory and how much memory they consume, below the progress bar and above the event log console".
Done:
- main.gd: a system's pieces are jobs in a queue (_piece / _pump_pieces / _make_piece): each planet and moon
  (a moon after its planet; placed from its orbit - _orbit_at - for the order), each station (other systems),
  each gate, the nav beacon, each nebula, the far planets, every saved or new ship and monster, each asteroid
  field, the mining crew (after the rocks), war fleets, travellers and live traders (after the stations and
  gates). Made nearest to the ship first, as many a frame as fit in 2.5 ms (PIECES_US), each fading in (0.4 s),
  each noted in the loading console. The scene runs from the start: only the core (ship, HUD, panels, quest,
  the player's state) is made before you fly - measured in a 60 Hz window: a new game 595 -> 150 ms still, a
  jump -> 146 ms, then 32-36 pieces stream in round you. Arriving by a gate: the gates first (you come out of
  one). Built directly (tests) every piece is made at once, as before. build_settled() = every piece in.
- Planet surfaces built ahead for every landable planet of the system (not only the nearest): one at a time,
  nearest first, kept (main.gd _surfaces, surface_ahead()); each in the memory pool as "surface:<id>", 44 MB
  (measured: five surfaces 199 MB of memory + 14 MB of textures), used more while you're near it; unloaded only
  if the pool runs out of room. The pool's usual need counts this system's surfaces (AssetPool.set_need_part).
  In a browser the nearest 3 only (WEB_SURFACES). Knossos: all 5 surfaces built ~22 s after a new game.
- The loading console (event_log.gd LoadBar, now a panel like the event log): its history with a scroll bar
  (up to 1000 lines, followed only while you're at the bottom, kept for the session across scenes), the pool's
  line, the progress bar (a planet built, the system streaming in - "Phaistos system: streaming in (12 / 36
  pieces)", the ground round you, the pictures; "All loaded" when done), and under it the memory map (MemMap):
  the pool's room as a strip, each kind of asset (AssetPool.KINDS: planet surfaces, anatomy, picture data,
  monsters, creatures, buildings and tiles, ships, stations, skies, effects, gates, citizens) an area as wide as
  its memory, in its colour, free room dark; hovering an area: how many, how much, its share, its 8 biggest
  assets with size and priority. The arrow left of the bar folds it to the bar alone (the pool's total at the
  bar's end) and opens it again. Always there (hidden only with the log, L).
- A surface built ahead no longer clears the event log's history or welcomes you again (the welcome lines were
  doubled - GameLog._built_ahead).
- Guide (game.md): the console, the memory map, streaming systems, surfaces built ahead.
- Doc shot space_hud: notes for the loading console and the memory map.
- Tests: test_play.test_system_streams_in (the scene runs while pieces come; all in at the end - every station,
  gate, planet; over several frames); test_surface_built_ahead uses surface_ahead().
Numbers: 32 pieces (Knossos) / 36 (Phaistos); 2.5 ms a frame; 150 ms still before flying (was 595); surface 44
MB; pool room 987 MB (Knossos: art + 5 surfaces), 1.5 GB in an 11-planet system.

## 2026-11-20 - The game no longer crashes as it closes; the Ship Computer's first open drawn ahead

- Quitting (from the title screen too) ended in "double free or corruption" - an abort: the memory pool's entries
  (static, holding calls bound to ProcArt) outlived ProcArt at exit. ProcArt empties the pool as it leaves
  (_exit_tree -> AssetPool.reset()).
- UI.dismantle frees the node itself at the frame's end (a surface taking itself apart was mid-call: "Object is
  locked" on taking off).
- The Ship Computer's unseen showing (prewarm) draws it at all but no opacity (0.01 - at 0 nothing's drawn, and its
  first Tab still drew everything for the first time: a 199 ms frame, 151 of it drawing) and plays its hexagon
  curtain once (every part drawn through the curtain's shader: those pipelines made ahead too).
Files: scripts/proc_art.gd, scripts/ui.gd, scripts/ship_menu.gd.

## 2026-11-20 - Procedural placeholders for every sprite first; the health gauge; the automaton's shield; streaming made lighter

Asked: "the placeholder is always a fully procedural sprite, low detail, simple shapes, it's always displayed first and
only when the asset is ready the raster sprite is displayed"; "give full priority to procedural low resolution assets
that can be created really fast and only when they are all loaded and displayed you load the final assets"; "replace
the shield and hull display with a new graphic: the outline of the current ship, filled with a water-like effect in red
for the hull, surrounded by a blue circle for the shield also filled with a water-like animation; add a shield also to
the automaton and a very similar gui; afflictions as icons around this circular gui, clockwise".
Done:
- PlaceholderArt (new, scripts/placeholder_art.gd): a placeholder per sprite, made procedurally - a simple shape for its
  kind (a hull with swept wings, a station's ring on spokes, a beast, a robed figure, an isometric block, a ring, a
  diamond, a glow, a sky band, a slab) in the sprite's own two main colours, fitted to its opaque box. Each kind's
  shape a 48 px mask drawn once; a placeholder = two masked blits (engine calls, no pixel loops).
- tools/sprite_sizes.py: sizes.json also holds each sprite's main colour, its shade and its opaque box (Pillow).
- ProcArt: first every sprite's placeholder (4 ms a frame - all 1093 in well under a second), noted in the loading
  console; only then the real pictures load (placeholders_done), each replacing its placeholder in place
  (ImageTexture.set_image: measured 0.15 ms a picture to read back). sprite() always answers at once (its
  placeholder if the picture isn't in). The placeholders are in the memory pool (pinned, ~10 MB; their own colour on
  the memory map).
- HealthGauge (new, scripts/health_gauge.gd; shaders/gauge_fill.gdshader, gauge_ring.gdshader): the ship's outline
  (its own sprite's silhouette, lit edge) filled with red liquid to the hull's share - a wavy moving surface, darker
  depth, a light band at the waterline, rising bubbles - inside a 150 px ring filled with blue liquid to the
  shields' share; the afflictions' badges round it clockwise from the top (30 degrees apart, AfflictionBar.icon_for);
  HULL / SHIELDS numbers under it. Space HUD: in place of the shield and hull bars (fuel and drachmas stay). Surface
  HUD: the automaton's outline (its front standing frame), HEALTH / SHIELD.
- The automaton's shield (surface_props.gd Pilot): 40 (+ gear "max_shield"), takes a hit before health and parts,
  recharges 12/s after 3 s out of the fight.
- Warmup: a HealthGauge (its two shaders compiled on the title).
- Streaming lighter: background work on the main thread paced by time (BgWork.take: 6% of each second - a 1 ms
  slice a frame had taken a 600 FPS frame from 1.1 to 2.3 ms); a surface built ahead: no path grid till you land,
  its scenery from the paced share with one worker, a chunk job every 40 ms at most; a surface taken apart stops
  streaming at once (errors gone). The loading console's history draws only the rows in view (a 1000-line label
  laid itself out again every second: 45 ms frames while planets were built).
- Guide: the health gauge, the automaton's shield, afflictions round the gauge. Doc shots space_hud (notes: the gauge,
  fuel and drachmas) and damage (afflictions round the gauge).
- Tests: test_damage_feedback (the gauge's icons; the automaton's shield soaks, breaks through, recharges);
  test_gear / test_repair empty the shield before testing hits.

## 2026-11-20 - Surfaces built ahead wait out of the tree (parked)

Found (A/B of the space FPS tour, building ahead off / on): keeping finished surfaces in the tree - hidden, stopped,
~2400 nodes each - still cost the frame (~11% in a window, measured by taking them out and putting them back).
Done: main.gd parks a built surface whose streaming has settled (streaming_idle) out of the tree, one per tick
(~11 ms); landing puts it back under the root (~9 ms, in the landing animation) before it takes the game's state;
a parked one that's dropped is freed directly. PlanetSurface._enter_tree redoes what leaving undid (its ground pump,
its lift drawing, the building culture).
Numbers (space tour, mean of 29 scenarios, building ahead on / off): 0.77 before parking, 0.88 after; a system whose
surfaces are done runs as fast as with none built ahead; a system just entered, its surfaces building: 20-35% under
for the minute or so that takes (6% of the main thread paced + the workers' share), a few 25-30 ms frames.
Files: scripts/main.gd, scripts/planet_surface.gd.
